title: Tin whistle
summary: A Clare D tin whistle built only from the published measurements of one real whistle (ISVR, Southampton): its bore, six finger-hole diameters and spacings, the tapered flue channel, the window, the wedge and the closed pocket behind the flue, blown at the air flow the same paper measured for each note of the scale, through a forced Bickley jet matched to the windway's exit. Speaks, except that the two highest overblown operating points do not reach their own register (A6 sounds the second and D7 the third, with the cited 12.5 ms onset ramp); not graded on the site. Four screened tin-whistle recordings now exist (Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0: A5 twice, D6 and G6), but the grader has no library for them yet, so the renders are listened to and nothing here claims to match a real whistle.
physics_present: fs-couple flue_loop: a jet driven by a blowing pressure that is computed from the published air flow of each note through the measured flue (Shah's laminar developing-flow law for a straight slit, refused outside its cited validity), with the measured window length as the jet length, acting on a connected duct network (one jet drives the whole graph). The jet's response is the forced Bickley jet (pexfp.135.4), matched to that windway's exit at each note's held pressure by Verge's rule as Segoufin states it (thesis, 2000, sec. 5.2): its centre speed is the exit's Bernoulli core speed (1.43 times the bulk speed on D5 down to 1.23 on D7c) and its half-width conserves the exit's momentum flux (0.44 to 0.56 of the flue height). The relay's band chain and authored displacement gain are not used
the measured cylindrical bore with six finger holes as plane-wave chimney sections on ideal junctions, open or closed per the published fingering chart, and the closed pocket behind the flue

the window's acoustic mass from its 3-D geometry: the 8 mm wide by 5.3 mm cut through the 2.4 mm wall of the 6.1 mm bore, its side walls parallel like the windway's, with the pocket behind it and free space outside, solved as potential flow on a staircase of cut cells (fs_bem::wall_window, three grids extrapolated at the order they show) and installed in place of the 0.61 a_eq mouth inertance. Where the wedge tip sits inside the wall is not published, so both ends of its bracket are rendered: a face straight through the wall, 17.84 mm of bore, and a 25 degree wedge from a tip 0.5 mm above the bore, 16.31 mm (the textbook law gives 12.80 mm). In native renders with one binary, against the radial cut they replace (15.71 mm, a lower bound), the straight face lowers the notes by 8 to 21 cents, 48 to 95 percent of the passive shift (F#5 the least), and the wedge by 2 to 6 cents

the measurement's gas: dry air at 20 C, because the paper blew the whistle from a regulated, metered air supply in a 20 C anechoic room, not by mouth (specimen.tsv). Breath temperature and humidity do not apply to this reference
fractional-delay propagation and gas-derived viscothermal loss on the long bore sections

radiation reaction and observation from the apertures themselves, so the sound is radiated pressure at a physical receiver rather than internal pressure: a compact baffled-piston load on every open hole and the open end, plus the window, which radiates from the outer face of the same 3-D solve on the head's rigid outer cylinder (resistance from the cylindrical-harmonic series, its static mass by Kramers-Kronig and taken out of the window mass, a passive chain of parallel R-L-C cells fitted from 20 Hz to 24 kHz within 1.4 % on the straight face) in place of an authored window loss

a self-sustained oscillation: each note settles to a steady tone and re-rendering with another jet seed gives the same pitch and level (shown on the relay jet these cards used before; the forced-jet renders use one seed), so it is a limit cycle and not a filtered seed
physics_missing: a measured jet that sustains this whistle: the opt-in published jet transfer (Price, Johnston and McKinnon 2015 Eqs. 4 to 10, with the jet gain they fitted with the pipe flow blocked and the long-channel phase velocity measured by de la Cuadra) does NOT self-sustain at any of the paper's four ladder flows: all four renders are silent after the attack (gate 2 of pexfp.320, build a3e8bc48f; the register ladder above belongs to the interim slot-jet card, not to a measured jet). The same hosted loop does sustain on two plain-tube fixtures of the real island (tests/flue_nolle_loop.rs), and the whistle loop is live, not open: with every loss removed it sounds at the very frequency the linear tool predicts, and its line shapes at all four flows follow the tool's open-loop shape. But its strength on the whistle is an order of magnitude or more below the linear tool's, so the tool's predicted instability at the two higher flows does not appear. The gap is unresolved; it does not depend on the network structure (riser, pocket, stubs), is not the passive loss (native pole widths agree with the analytic ones), not the one-sample lag, not the alpha_j term, not the viscous windway path, and the module alone behaves as the tool says. The playing-condition jet gain is UNKNOWN (u-jet-playing-gain), so this is not a claim about a real whistle

a graded comparison: four screened whistle recordings exist (Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0: A5 twice, D6 and G6) but the grader's library is built from UIowa-named files and holds none of them, so no pair is graded and no claim of resemblance is made. The cards also model the ISVR rig, not a player: it was blown from a metered 20 C air supply, which is why the bore holds dry air. A played whistle carries breath, which would raise every note by about 11 cents (measured on the pan-pipe cards) and the jet speed at a fixed pressure by about 1 percent (unknowns u-played-bore-gas). Measured with the origin grader's functions against those clips (no ruler, so numbers and not verdicts; the source is marked not gradable in the reference index), the forced-jet renders' spectral gap is 35.4 to 35.7 dB on A5 (39.9 to 40.2 on the relay) and 38.0 dB on D6 (41.7), their odd-even gap 44 and 39 dB (80 and 83 on the relay; the clips' own odd-even level is 6 to 8 dB), and they sit 16 to 19 cents (A5) and 27 cents (D6) flat of the clips

the register ladder: on the forced jet with the cited 12.5 ms onset ramp, the all-holes-closed fingering at the paper's second, third and fourth register flows sounds the second, the second and the third register. D6c sounds the second register at once (the previous 50 ms ramp held it in the first for 0.45 s); A6c sounds the second register, D6, 703 cents below its note (as at 50 ms); D7c sounds the third register, 1749 Hz, 511 cents below its note (the second, 1180 Hz, 1192 cents below, at 50 ms). So the ladder defect stays on A6c (the target is the third) and D7c (the fourth), D7c one register nearer. A 19.1 ms ramp, the other end of the bracket of recorder medians (u-attack-spread), gives the same registers, with D7c's second register lingering above 40 percent of its final amplitude for the first 70 ms. The 12.5 and 19.1 ms renders use the cards' straight window face only. At the previous 50 ms ramp all three sounded the second register (A6c and D7c on both window ends); there the relay jet these cards used before reached the second, third and fourth modes within 16 cents, and a Poiseuille exit on the same forced jet reached the second on A6c and the third on D7c. The developing exit's jet is slower (centre speed 1.23 to 1.31 times the bulk speed on these notes, against 1.5 for a Poiseuille exit), which moves them down. The four notes the site plays (D5, G5, B5, D6) keep the pitch (to 0.1 cent), harmonic line ratios (to 0.1 dB) and level (to 0.01 dB) of the 50 ms cards over 0.8 to 1.6 s, compared to that precision and not sample by sample, and their attack arrives 34 to 40 ms earlier. E5, F#5, A5, C#6 and the four nolle gate files were not rendered at 12.5 ms. Not claimed: any resemblance to a played whistle, any grade, the saturation mechanism, or that 12.5 ms is a whistle player's value (it is a recorder value taken by analogy). No parameter was adjusted: the ramp's value comes from the source and was fixed before any render at it

the register transitions themselves: only the paper's measured operating points were rendered, each from rest with the same onset ramp. The flow at which each register begins, the hysteresis between rising and falling flow and the effect of how fast the breath rises are not mapped. On the same whistle geometry the lip-jet card does not stage (it is silent at the lowest measured flow and stays in the first register at the three higher flows, at two mechanics clocks), so the relay's ladder belonged to the windway-jet card and not to the geometry alone
the second-octave D of the scale files is the first register of the pipe with only the top hole open (the paper's cleaner fingering), not an overblown note

a spectrum like a real whistle: on the forced jet the even harmonics are 61 to 68 dB below the fundamental on D5 to C#6 and 43 to 50 dB on the second-register notes (100 dB or more on the relay), where a real whistle has a smooth fall of all harmonics. The jet cut is symmetric because the labium offset and jet angle are not published and are set to zero (UNKNOWN). The share above 2.8 kHz is 0.02 to 0.13 on D5 to C#6 (0.02 to 0.39 on the relay) and 0.49 to 0.71 on D6 and D6c

the energy above 5 kHz: on the forced jet the A5 and D6 renders still carry 24 to 26 dB (A5) and 25 dB (D6) more energy above 5 kHz than the screened U4 whistle recordings, in the grader's share (A5 -19.6 dB against -43.4 and -45.7, D6 -11.0 dB against -36.1; the relay jet 30 to 32 dB and 26 dB), because the radiated harmonics H7 to H17 sit at -19 to -38 dB re H1 where the recordings fall to -57 to -82 dB (H3 is 3 dB low on A5 and 18 dB high on D6). Measured on the relay cards with the card's own switches, the bore wall loss carries 0.3 dB (A5) and 0.5 dB (D6) of the band, the window's other documented radiation operator 0.0 dB, and the receiver only the physical frequency weighting (the radiated share follows from the aperture flows to 0.7 and 1.1 dB). On the forced jet the window aperture still carries 67 percent (A5) and 76 percent (D6) of the radiated 5 to 16 kHz power, the open end 22 percent, the four holes 11.5 percent on A5 and the one hole 2 percent on D6, and the band lies on harmonics of the played pitch. The window flow has no jump on the forced jet (no sample changes by more than 0.9 percent of its peak-to-peak on A5 and 1.7 percent on D6, against 9.6 percent on the relay) but a corner, a change of slope at two phases of the cycle half a period apart (inferred to be the jet's two crossings of the labium edge), so its harmonics fall only as 1/n^1.6 to 1/n^2: -36 dB (A5) and -38 dB (D6) re the fundamental at n=7. Replacing the relay jet by the forced Bickley jet takes 6 dB off A5's share and 1 dB off D6's, so the relay's saturation is not what carries the content. The jet displacement at the labium is not exposed by the observation tap, so the cause is not isolated beyond the jet-to-window flow (diagnosis on bead pexfp.338)

pitch: on the forced jet with the straight window face the notes land from -28 to +14 cents of the tempered values (D5 -17, E5 -15, F#5 -28, G5 -7, A5 -9, B5 +14, C#6 +11, D6 -5, overblown D6 -18), with the wedge from -16 to +29 cents (D5 -8, E5 -6, F#5 -16, G5 +5, A5 +5, B5 +29, C#6 +28, D6 +7, overblown D6 -9), still sharper as more holes open. That is 7 to 68 cents flatter than the relay jet (straight face -16 to +40 cents; F#5 moves the most) and 1.3 to 2.8 cents flatter than a Poiseuille exit on the same forced jet. On the relay the window's radiation moved the notes by +7 to -42 cents. The plane-wave chimney on an ideal junction has no hole inertance corrections or interaction between holes (the paper's own hole model has them), the window has no viscous edge loss and no baffle beyond the head's own outer cylinder, and the wedge's place in the wall is a bracket, so no pitch claim is made

the jet: the forced jet's base profile is Bickley, and a developing exit is flatter (de la Cuadra's Nolle fits, n 2 to 4); 1 h past a 10 mm by 1 mm flue those fits give a momentum-equivalent half-width 0.13 to 0.16 h wider than the rule. The exit is held at each note's pressure, so attack and release are not covered. The jet card is still the repository's interim slot-jet card of a lattice rig, outside its Reynolds band

labium offset and jet angle: not published, neutral. The onset ramp is a recorder value taken by analogy, not a whistle player's: 12.5 ms linear, the experienced recorder players' median 10 ms mouth-pressure rise (10 to 90 percent, Ernoult and Fabre 2017) divided by 0.8, reaching the voice as a 1 kHz staircase of about 13 steps (u-onset-control-staircase); its spread, its shape and the windway's inertia are unknowns (u-attack-recorder-analogy, u-attack-spread, u-attack-shape, u-attack-windway-inertia)

the true flue taper (the windway law uses the exit depth over the whole length, which most likely overstates the loss), the pocket shape (a cylinder, an upper bound), the thin hole wall (a numerical floor on the hole length replaces it), the chord reduction of the bore at the wedge, hole shape and undercut
breath noise, the chiff of the attack and any edge-tone noise: the renders are tonal
native verification of the forced-jet renders beyond one mechanics clock and one jet seed (D5 renders bit-identically at jet histories of 65536 and 131072 samples)
